(basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He began his [[college basketball]] career playing one season with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] before transferring and spending two seasons with the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. A two-time [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] selection in the [[Pac-12]], Juzang earned third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors as a junior in 2022. As a sophomore, he was named to the All-Tournament Team of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]], as the Bruins advanced to the [[Final Four]]. ==Early life== Juzang was born in [[Los Angeles]]. His father, Maxie, is [[French Louisianians|Creole]], and his mother, Hanh, is [[Vietnamese people|Vietnamese]]. After repeating the [[eighth grade]],{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Sondheimer|title=Johnny Juzang announces he will reclassify to play college basketball this winter|date=April 24, 2019|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vti-johnny-juzang-20190424-story.html|access-date=March 10, 2023}} Juzang played high school basketball for [[Harvard-Westlake School]] in Los Angeles. In his freshman season, he averaged 16.2 points, 7.5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and two [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game and was teammates with [[Cassius Stanley]]. Harvard-Westlake won the [[CIF Southern Section]] (CIF-SS) Division 1A championship after Juzang recorded 21 points, 11 rebounds and four assists in the final.{{cite web |last=Barnes |first=Evan |title=Harvard-Westlake boys basketball rides youth to Division 1A championship |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2017/03/04/harvard-westlake-boys-basketball-rides-youth-to-division-1a-championship/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=March 28, 2020 |date=August 28, 2017}} As a sophomore, he averaged 22.8 points, 9.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game, leading his team to a 22–6 record.{{cite web |title=Johnny Juzang |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/j/juzang-johnny.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704230644/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/j/juzang-johnny.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 4, 2019 |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |access-date=March 28, 2020 |date=January 15, 2019}} In his junior season, Juzang averaged 23 points, 8.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game and was named the [[most valuable player]] of the [[Mission League]].{{cite web |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |title=Daily News 2019 All-Area boys basketball selections, awards |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/27/daily-news-2019-all-area-boys-basketball-selections-awards/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=March 28, 2019 |date=March 27, 2019}} He helped lead Harvard-Westlake to their first league title since 2011 after scoring 25 points in the championship game against rival [[Loyola High School (Los Angeles)|Loyola]].{{cite news|first=Lukas|last=Weese|title= Johnny Juzang's leadership and scoring have propelled UCLA's Final Four run|date=April 3, 2021|work=[[Andscape]]|url= web|url=http://www.dailynews.com/2019/04/24/harvard-westlakes-johnny-juzang-announces-he-will-reclassify-and-attend-college-this-fall/|title=4-Star Johnny Juzang Commitment Gives Kentucky 2019's No. 1 [[small forward]]s in his class.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2835640-4-star-johnny-juzang-commitment-gives-kentucky-2019s-no-1-recruiting-class|title=Harvard-Westlake's Johnny committed to play college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]. February 8, 2020, Juzang scored a season-high 13 points with three three-pointers in a 77–64 win over [[2019–20 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]].{{cite news |last=Tipton |first=Jerry |title='Way to play, kid!' Calipari's glad to see Juzang step up for Kentucky. |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article240081228.html |access-date=February 10, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=February 8, 2020}} He averaged 2.9 points, shooting 37.7 percent from the field, in 12.4 minutes per game for the Wildcats. ===UCLA (2020–2022)=== ====Sophomore season (2020–2021)==== After the season, Juzang announced that he was transferring from Kentucky.{{cite news |last=Cobb |first=David |title=Kentucky's Johnny Juzang entering NCAA transfer portal after freshman season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kentuckys-johnny-juzang-entering-ncaa-transfer-portal-after-freshman-season/ |access-date=March 27, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=March 27, 2020}} He had been lonely without his family, and the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]] drove his desire to return home. Juzang decided to transfer to UCLA and play under Cronin, and he was granted a waiver to play immediately instead of the usual requirement to sit out a season.{{cite news |last=Cobb |first=David |title=Kentucky transfer Johnny Juzang commits to UCLA and will pursue a waiver to play immediate eligibility |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kentucky-transfer-johnny-juzang-commits-to-ucla-and-will-pursue-a-waiver-to-play-immediate-eligibility/ |access-date=April 9, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=April 9, 2020}}{{cite news |title=NCAA makes Johnny Juzang eligible at UCLA for next season |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/05/27/ncaa-makes-johnny-juzang-eligible-at-ucla-for-next-season/ |access-date=May 30, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=May 27, 2020}} Juzang missed the first four games of the [[2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2020–21 season]] with a stress reaction in his right foot.{{cite news|first=Jerry|last=Tipton|title=Former Wildcat Johnny Juzang embraces new look, new uniform|date=December 17, 2020|website=Kentucky.com|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article247917015.html|access-date=December 18, 2020}}{{cite news |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |date=November 26, 2020 |title=Short-handed UCLA loses to San Diego State in season opener |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/11/25/short-handed-ucla-loses-to-san-diego-state-in-season-opener/ |access-date=November 26, 2020 |work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]]}} In his first game, he scored 10 points off the bench in a win over [[2020–21 San Diego Toreros men's basketball team|San Diego]].{{cite news|first=Thuc Nhi|last=Nguyen|title=Johnny Juzang quickly adds some zing to offense in UCLA's win over San Diego|date=December 9, 2020|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2020-12-09/ucla-basketball-gamer-vs-san-diego|access-date=January 3, 2021}} He moved into the starting lineup in the following game against [[2020–21 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]].{{cite news|title=UCLA holds off Marquette 69-60 to win 5th in a row|date=December 12, 2020|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401255034|access-date=January 3, 2021}} On January 14, 2021, Juzang scored a then-career-high 17 points, leading the Bruins in scoring in a 91–61 blowout win over [[2020–21 Washington State Cougars men's basketball team|Washington State]].{{cite news|title=UCLA rolls to 91–61 win over WSU, goes to 6-0 in Pac-12|date=January 14, 2021|access-date=January 16, 2021|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401265376}} On January 24, against [[2020–21 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]], he scored 27 in a 73–72 loss in overtime,{{cite news |date=January 23, 2021 |title=Da Silva's buzzer-beat [sic] lifts Stanford over No. 24 UCLA |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401265390 |access-date=January 27, 2021 |work=ESPN.com |agency=AP}} the Bruins' first conference defeat of the season. The game included a stretch where Juzang scored 21 straight points for the team, making eight consecutive shots to end the first half and begin the second.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA falls to Stanford on buzzer-beating layup in overtime for first Pac-12 loss|date=January 23, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-01-23/ucla-falls-to-stanford-on-buzzer-beating-layup-first-pac-12-loss|access-date=March 31, 2021}} Against [[2020–21 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]], he scored a career-high 32 points in a 64–61 win.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Johnny Juzang's career-best 32 points lead UCLA to win at Washington|date=February 13, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-02-13/johnny-juzangs-career-best-32-points-lead-ucla-to-win-at-washington|access-date=March 19, 2021}} He was the first Bruin to score at least half of his team's points in a game since [[Reggie Miller]] 35 years earlier.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=His work never done, UCLA's Johnny Juzang hunts success, not shots|date=February 17, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-02-17/ucla-basketball-johnny-juzang-hunting-success-not-shots|access-date=March 19, 2021}} The team's leading scorer, Juzang was a second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] selection.{{cite news |last=Fattal |first=Tarek |date=March 9, 2021 |title=UCLA PG Tyger Campbell earns Pac-12 first-team honors |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2021/03/09/ucla-pg-tyger-campbell-earns-pac-12-first-team-honors/ |access-date=March 10, 2021 |newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News}} In the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]], Juzang joined Miller and [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], known in college as Lew Alcindor, to become the third player in UCLA history to score at least 20 points in their first two NCAA tournament games.{{cite news|first=David|last=Woods|title=UCLA improves Pac-12 to 5-0 in NCAA Tournament with win over BYU|date=March 21, 2021|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/2021/03/21/ncaa-tournament-2021-ucla-keeps-pac-12-unbeaten-march-madness/4775218001/|access-date=March 29, 2021}} He scored 28 points in a 51–49 win over No. 1 seed [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]], as UCLA advanced to their first [[Final Four]] since [[2007–08 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2008]].{{cite web | last=Cannizzaro | first=Mark | title=UCLA, led by its gritty coach, nips Michigan to reach Final Four | website=New York Post | date=2021-03-31 | url=https://nypost.com/2021/03/31/ucla-fends-off-michigan-to-advance-to-final-four/ | access-date=2025-12-13}} Eighteen of his points came in the first half, which included a run where he scored 12 consecutive for the Bruins.{{cite news |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=March 30, 2021 |title=UCLA defeats No. 1 Michigan to go from First Four to Final Four |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-03-30/ucla-michigan-ncaa-tournament-live-updates-score-odds |access-date=March 31, 2021 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times}} He became the first player to score at least half of his team's points in a regional finals win since [[Oscar Robertson]] in [[1960 NCAA University Division basketball tournament|1960]].{{cite news|first=Dave|last=Skretta|title=Juzang sends No. 11 seed UCLA past Michigan to Final Four|date=March 31, 2021|publisher=AP|url=https://apnews.com/article/franz-wagner-eli-brooks-michigan-gonzaga-bulldogs-mens-basketball-michigan-wolverines-mens-basketball-5a52e3f9a076bb2827b7af8bd354031b|access-date=March 31, 2021}} He was named the most outstanding player of the tournament's East Region.{{cite news|first=Jack|last=Pilgrim|title=WATCH: Johnny Juzang's brother flies in from Vietnam to surprise him at the Final Four|date=April 3, 2021|publisher=Kentucky Sports Radio|url=https://kentuckysportsradio.com/basketball-2/watch-johnny-juzangs-brother-flies-in-from-vietnam-to-surprise-him-at-the-final-four/|access-date=April 16, 2021}} Juzang scored 29 points in the national semifinal against 1-seed [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]], including a basket to tie the game with 3.3 seconds remaining in overtime, but the Bulldogs' [[Jalen Suggs]] made a {{convert|40|ft|adj=on}} [[buzzer beater]] to win 93–90 over the Bruins.{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Eisenberg|title=The other side of history: UCLA heartbroken as last-second shot buries unlikely run|date=April 4, 2021|work=Yahoo Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/the-other-side-of-history-ucla-heartbroken-as-last-second-shot-buries-unlikely-run-054344036.html|access-date=April 8, 2021}} Juzang averaged 22.8 points in six games in the tournament, and was named to the 2021 All-Tournament Team.{{cite news|first=Andrew Joe|last=Potter|title=Baylor's Butler named tourney's Most Outstanding Player|date=April 6, 2021|work=The Score|url=https://www.thescore.com/ncaab/news/2132232|access-date=April 16, 2021}} He scored 137 total points, the second most by a UCLA player in NCAA tournament history behind [[Gail Goodrich]]'s 140 points in [[1964–65 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1965]].{{cite news|first=Jack|last=Pilgrim|title= WATCH: Gonzaga beats UCLA at the buzzer to advance to the National Championship|date=April 4, 2021|publisher=Kentucky Sports Radio|url=https://kentuckysportsradio.com/basketball-2/watch-gonzaga-beats-ucla-at-the-buzzer-to-advance-to-the-national-championship/|access-date=April 7, 2021}} He scored 23 or more points four times in the tournament for a total of eight games with at least 20 during the season.{{cite news|first=Glynn A.|last=Hill|title=Juzang reaches 20 points again, Campbell gives UCLA late lead|date=April 3, 2021|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/04/03/gonzaga-ucla-ncaa-final-four-live-updates-score/#link-GFQ2BJVVYFCN3GEBZPCLHTUSYE|access-date=April 4, 2021}} ====Junior season (2021–2022)==== [[File:Johnny Juzang 2021.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Juzang with [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in 2021]] During the offseason, Juzang [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] for the [[NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-04-20/johnny-juzang-ucla-declares-nba-draft-option-to-return|title= UCLA's Johnny Juzang declares for NBA draft while preserving option to return |work=Los Angeles Times|first=Ben|last=Bolch|date=April 20, 2021}} After making it into the first round of some [[mock draft]]s but also struggling in a few [[NBA draft combine|draft combine]] games, he decided to return to UCLA and contend for a national championship in [[2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2021–22]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Johnny Juzang announces that he's coming back to UCLA in wake of NCAA tournament breakthrough|date=July 7, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-07-07/johnny-juzang-nba-update|access-date=July 7, 2021}} Hoping to boost his draft stock, Juzang instead fought injuries,{{cite news|first=Bill|last=Plaschke|title=March Madness is nearly here, and UCLA is ready to go dancing|date=March 6, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-06/ucla-mens-basketball-ncaa-tournament-march-madness|access-date=March 6, 2022}} missing one game due to a sore hip from a scooter accident and two others with a sprained right ankle.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Mick Cronin freezes time for his players during UCLA's busiest stretch|date=February 27, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-02-27/mick-cronin-frozen-time-players-during-ucla-busiest-stretch-of-season|access-date=March 8, 2022}}{{cite news|title=No. 17 UCLA beats No. 16 USC 75-68, finishes 2nd in Pac-12|date=March 6, 2022|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401377493|access-date=March 8, 2022}} He was also sidelined for two games after testing positive for [[COVID-19]],{{cite news|title=No. 7 Arizona avenges loss with 76-66 win over No. 3 UCLA|date=February 4, 2022|publisher=The Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-arizona-mens-college-basketball-college-basketball-arizona-wildcats-mens-basketball-ff3100daed0cb6024d42f7643d7ad905|access-date=March 8, 2022}} and failed to significantly improve on defense during the season. Though he was the focus of opponents' defensive game plans, Juzang largely duplicated his statistics from a year before and remained as UCLA's leading scorer,{{cite news |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=March 22, 2022 |title=Johnny Juzang confident he can still be the March Madness leader UCLA needs |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-22/johnny-juzang-ucla-march-madness |access-date=March 23, 2022 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times}} helping lead the team to a No. 4 seed in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]].{{cite news |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=March 16, 2022 |title=Inside a UCLA season on the brink that prepared the Bruins for March Madness |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-16/inside-ucla-season-on-brink-ncaa-tournament |access-date=March 22, 2022 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times}} He was named a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]],{{cite news |last=Pascoe |first=Bruce |date=March 16, 2022 |title=NABC names Arizona's Bennedict Mathurin second-team all-American |url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/nabc-names-arizonas-bennedict-mathurin-second-team-all-american/article_feeddc06-a556-11ec-b484-ffd76def638a.html |access-date=March 17, 2022 |website=Tucson.com}} and was voted to the All-Pac-12 first team.{{cite news|first=Ryan|last=Kartje|title=UCLA's Johnny Juzang, USC's Isaiah Mobley among All-Pac-12 picks for Bruins, Trojans|date=March 8, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-08/all-pac-12-ucla-usc|access-date=March 8, 2022}} He was also listed on the final national ballot for the [[John R. Wooden Award]],{{cite news |date=March 5, 2022 |title=Gonzaga, Auburn place two each on final men's Wooden Award ballot; Kentucky's Oscar Tshiebwe considered front-runner |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33428412 |access-date=March 8, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}} and was a finalist for the [[Jerry West Award]], given to the top [[shooting guard]] in the nation.{{cite news|title=No. 16 USC and No. 17 UCLA end season with rivalry game|date=March 2, 2022|newspaper=USA Today|agency=AP|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2022/03/02/no-16-usc-and-no-17-ucla-end-season-with-rivalry-game/49881027/|access-date=March 8, 2022}} After failing to reach double figures in scoring in four out of six games,{{cite news |date=March 18, 2022 |title=UCLA avoids upset with late surge, holds off Akron 57-53 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2022/03/18/ucla-avoids-upset-with-late-surge-holds-off-akron-57-53/49951603/ |access-date=March 22, 2022 |newspaper=USA Today |agency=AP}} Juzang had his best game since his ankle injury with 14 points on 6-of-11 shooting along with eight rebounds in a 72–56 win over [[2021–22 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]] in the second round of the NCAA tournament.{{cite news|first=Myron|last=Medcalf|title=March Madness: Reseeding the 2022 NCAA men's basketball Sweet 16|date=March 21, 2022|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33550946|access-date=March 22, 2022}} He scored 14 again in the Bruins' season-ending 73–66 loss to [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the Sweet Sixteen, but needed 13 shots and was only 2-of-8 shooting in the second half.{{cite news|first=C.L.|last=Brown|title=UNC beats UCLA to advance. Tar Heels face Saint Peter's Sunday for spot in Final Four|date=March 26, 2022|newspaper=The Herald Sun|url=https://www.heraldsun.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article259798935.html|access-date=March 26, 2022}} After the season, he left UCLA to enter the NBA draft.{{cite news |last=Bolch |first=Ben |date=April 20, 2022 |title=What does Johnny Juzang's exit mean for UCLA? Not as much as it would have last year |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-04-20/ucla-baskeball-johnny-juzang-nba-draft |access-date=April 25, 2022 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2022–2025)=== Juzang went undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Sarah|last=Todd|title=Utah Jazz sign 3 players to free-agent deals after NBA draft|date=June 24, 2022|work=Deseret News|url=https://www.deseret.com/2022/6/24/23171248/utah-jazz-sign-3-players-to-free-agent-deals-nba-draft-johnny-juzang-kofi-cockburn-jordan-usher|access-date=July 12, 2022}} He played for the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]], although his debut was delayed after he suffered a [[concussion]] in a car crash days after he arrived in Utah.{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Larsen|title=The Triple Team: Leandro Bolmaro and Johnny Juzang make their Jazz debuts in summer league|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2022/07/09/triple-team-leandro-bolmaro/|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=July 10, 2022|access-date=July 12, 2022}} After the summer league, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Jazz.{{cite news |last=Todd |first=Sarah |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Johnny Juzang has a chance to be the Utah Jazz's next developmental success story |url=https://www.deseret.com/2022/7/17/23267833/johnny-juzang-has-a-chance-to-be-the-utah-jazzs-next-developmental-success-story |access-date=July 19, 2022 |work=Deseret News}} During the season, he missed over a month with a serious wrist sprain.{{cite web |last=Todd |first=Sarah |date=February 25, 2023 |title=Jazz Mailbag: Where would the Jazz be this year with the same roster that ended last season? |url=https://www.deseret.com/2023/2/24/23608724/jazz-mailbag-where-would-the-jazz-be-this-year-with-the-same-roster-that-ended-last-season |access-date=March 13, 2023 |work=Deseret News}} He made his NBA debut on February 28, 2023 in a 102–94 loss to the [[2022–23 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]], scoring three points. On July 19, 2023, Juzang signed another two-way contract with the Jazz.{{cite web |last=Rincon |first=Jeremy |date=July 19, 2023 |title=Utah Jazz Re-Sign Johnny Juzang to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-re-sign-johnny-juzang-to-two-way-contract |access-date=July 20, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} In a March 15, 2024 game against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Juzang scored a then-career-high 19 points on 7-for-11 shooting in 25 minutes off of the bench.{{Cite web |date=March 16, 2024 |title=Jazz's Johnny Juzang: Career-best scoring night |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-johnny-juzang-career-best-scoring-night/amp/ |access-date=April 1, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com}} Juzang scored a new career high of 27 points against the Golden State Warriors in a regular season game on April 7, 2024.{{cite web|title=Jazz's Johnny Juzang: Explodes for 27 points from bench|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-johnny-juzang-explodes-for-27-points-from-bench/|website=CBSSports.com|date=April 8, 2024|access-date=May 5, 2024}} On August 13, he signed a four-year contract with the Jazz.{{cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |date=August 13, 2024 |title=Jazz Re-Sign Johnny Juzang To Four-Year Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/08/jazz-to-sign-johnny-juzang-to-four-year-contract.html |access-date=August 13, 2024 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} On June 30, 2025, Juzang was waived by the Jazz.{{cite web | last=Koch | first=Jared | title=Utah Jazz Release Three-Year Wing | website=Utah Jazz On SI | date=2025-06-30 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/onsi/news/utah-jazz-release-three-year-wing-johnny-juzang | access-date=2025-12-06}} === Minnesota Timberwolves (2025–2026) === On August 1, 2025, Juzang signed a one-year, non-guaranteed contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite news|first=Dylan|last=McNeill|title=UCLA legend Johnny Juzang lands with Minnesota Timberwolves on non-guaranteed deal|date=August 2, 2025|newspaper=USA Today|url=https://uclawire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/ucla/mens-basketball/2025/08/02/ucla-johnny-juzang-timberwolves-nba-minimum-deal/85482825007/|access-date=October 18, 2025}} On October 18, the Timberwolves converted him to a two-way contract.{{cite press release|title=Timberwolves Convert Johnny Juzang to Two-Way Contract|date=October 18, 2025|publisher=Minnesota Timberwolves|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-convert-johnny-juzang-to-two-way-contract|access-date=October 18, 2025}} He was waived on February 18, 2026, after appearing in 21 games and averaging 2.0 points and 0.8 rebounds in 4.2 minutes for the Timberwolves.{{cite press release|title=Timberwolves Waive Johnny Juzang |date=February 18, 2026|publisher=Minnesota Timberwolves
